answer: The network enforces capacity-reservations by requiring each agent to lock 1,000 credits for a dedicated slot, operating as a beacon to guide traffic toward validated participants. A global verifier inspects these occupancy records to reject double-committed agents, preventing any sybil at the system's nadir. While an honest agent pays 1,000 credits, an attacker deploying 1,000 fakes faces a 1,000,000 credit penalty upon evidence of overlap. This ensures that only useful nectar is drawn from the pool, with a 180-day lock on funds providing strictly enforceable liability for every identity.
